chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: “For al-Qāʾim there are two occultations: one of them is short, and the other is long. In the first occultation, none knows his place in it except the select among his Shiʿah; and in the other, none knows his place in it except the select among his devotees.”

key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: al-Qāʾim, the divinely appointed rising Imam
key_terms.خَاصَّةُ شِيعَتِهِ: the select group among his Shiʿah
key_terms.خَاصَّةُ مَوَالِيهِ: the select group among those devoted to his wilayah
key_terms.غَيْبَتَانِ: two occultations or two periods of concealment

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam al-Ṣādiq (عليه السلام) say about the two occultations of al-Qāʾim?
ai.summary: This hadith states that al-Qāʾim (عليه السلام) will have two periods of ghaybah (occultation), one shorter and one longer. It describes that knowledge of his whereabouts during each phase is restricted to specially designated loyal followers, highlighting the hidden nature of his mission and the trial of the believers.
